ai.description: The Waynaad Day Gecko reaches a snout-vent length of 40 mm. It is brown with a distinct pale vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Key features include granular scales and a slender, flattened body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis monticola* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along its flanks, which are absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: The Waynaad Day Gecko inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks at elevations between 700 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Waynaad Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rocky outcrops and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis monticola* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, extending from June through September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis monticola* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting rocky areas at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
